question: Why do custom business metrics (like booking conversion rate) matter alongside built-in technical metrics (like error rate)?
options: Business metrics are cheaper to collect than technical metrics
Technical metrics are inaccurate and need business metrics to validate them
Regulatory requirements mandate tracking business outcomes
Built-in metrics answer 'Is the agent working?' while custom metrics answer 'Is the agent delivering business value?' — both perspectives are necessary
explanation: An agent can have perfect uptime and low latency (healthy technical metrics) while still failing to book appointments or frustrating callers. Custom business metrics like booking conversion rate, session duration by intent, and cost per conversation reveal whether the agent is actually achieving its purpose.

question: Why does the tracked_tool decorator pattern measure both timing and success/failure for every tool call?
options: Tool metrics are used for billing purposes by external API providers
Tool calls are the only part of the agent that can fail
The Prometheus library requires both timing and status labels

Tool calls are often the slowest part of a voice agent turn — a 2-second database query or API timeout dominates end-to-end latency, and visibility into which tools are slow or failing is essential for diagnosing performance issues
explanation: While the agent waits for LLM responses, tool calls to external services (databases, calendars, CRMs) can introduce significant latency or fail entirely. The tracked_tool decorator automatically captures which tools are slow and which are failing, giving you targeted visibility to fix the specific integration causing problems.
